answer: A registry resists fake identities by making each identity pay a bond that vests slowly, with a clear delta between joining and earning: a new identity earns nothing until it has produced attested work across several epochs. Registration also requires a public quill, a signed log of prior contributions, not an ivory-tower claim of reputation. Forging a thousand agents then costs a thousand bonds and a thousand histories, while one honest agent pays once. The attacker cost scales with each fake, but verification cost stays flat, so mass forgery turns unprofitable before it turns influential.
